> **Experiment 1-2 ★: Kimi K3 Native Agent Capability**
>
> This experiment demonstrates the native Agent capability of **Kimi K3**, an example of the “Model as Agent” paradigm. Kimi K3 is a Mixture of Experts (MoE) model with approximately 2.8 trillion parameters. MoE can be viewed as a team of experts: for each kind of problem, the system activates only the few experts best suited to it rather than the entire model, preserving capability without paying the full efficiency cost. Kimi K3 has a 1 million token context window, native visual understanding, and an always-on “thinking mode.” Through reinforcement learning, it has internalized the tool-calling **decision policy** as a native capability: when to call a tool, which tool to call, and what arguments to pass are all decided by the model, allowing it to carry out tasks such as web searches autonomously. To be precise, what is internalized is the *when and how to call* decision; the tools themselves, such as `web_search` and `code_runner`, still execute server-side as API-level built-in tools. Kimi runs these official tools through a server-side script engine called Formula.
>
> The key observations are that the model decides when to search and what to search for, showing genuine autonomy; it adjusts strategy as search results arrive and judges whether it has enough information. A common misconception is worth clarifying: **reinforcement learning gives the model the decision policy**, not the tools themselves. It teaches when to call a tool, which tool to choose, what arguments to pass, whether to continue after receiving a result, and how to chain dozens or hundreds of calls into coherent reasoning; these *whether-and-how-to-use* judgments are what get written into the model's weights. **The tools and their execution are provided by the Agent framework or API built-ins**: the implementations of `web_search` and `code_runner`, the code sandbox, and the infrastructure that issues calls and returns results all live outside the model. RL optimizes the decision policy; it does not embed a search engine or a code sandbox into the model's weights. Thus, the orchestration loop has not disappeared; it has moved from the client to the server, while decision-making has moved into the model[^ch1-2].
>
> [^ch1-2]: Thanks to reader asdlem for pointing out and clarifying, via GitHub Issue #30, the distinction that what RL internalizes is the tool-calling decision policy, not the tool execution mechanism. See https://github.com/bojieli/ai-agent-book/issues/30
>
> Kimi K3’s notable advantage in Agent tasks is **the stability of long-chain tool calls**—it can sustain 200–300 consecutive tool calls with coherent reasoning throughout, far beyond the few dozen calls at which most models begin to degrade. K3 is optimized for long-horizon programming and Agent workloads, and was released in two variants: K3 Max (for dialogue and Agent tasks) and K3 Swarm Max (for large-scale parallel processing). As an open-source model, it matches top-tier closed-source systems on software engineering and Agent benchmarks—evidence that reinforcement learning can endow a model with native Agent capability.
>
> **Experiment 1-3 ★: GPT-5.6 Native Deep Research Capability**
>
> The second experiment uses **OpenAI GPT-5.6** to show how an advanced model, backed by API-level built-in tools, closes the "search—read—analyze" orchestration loop on the server side for Deep Research. One convenient GPT-5.6 feature is **Freeform Tool Calling**. Traditionally, a model calling a tool must serialize every parameter into strict JSON (a structured data format), much like filling out a form with rigid formatting rules. Freeform tool calling (declared in the API through a tool of `type: "custom"`) lets the model send raw text straight to the tool (a snippet of Python code, a SQL query), avoiding JSON escaping entirely. It is worth stressing that this is an evolution of the API's parameter format, not an innovation in model architecture—the client's tool-calling loop (detect `tool_calls` → execute → return the result) stays the same; only the arguments change from a JSON string to raw text.
>
> GPT-5.6, paired with the Responses API's **web search and code interpreter** built-in tools, delivers the core mechanism of Deep Research: the model can autonomously search the web for real-time information and write code for in-depth analysis, enabling an iterative research process of "search -> read -> analyze -> search again." For example, when faced with a question like "What is the shortest distance between the capitals of the 10 ASEAN countries?", GPT-5.6 automatically searches for the geographic coordinates of each capital, then writes Python code to calculate the great-circle distance between all pairs of capitals, ultimately identifying the closest pair. Similarly, in a task like "Search for Bitcoin's trend over the past month and perform technical analysis," it can fetch real-time price data from multiple financial data sources, use professional technical analysis libraries to calculate moving averages, RSI, MACD, and other technical indicators, generate visual charts, and provide trading recommendations.
>
> More importantly, GPT-5.6 internalizes the design philosophy of the **OpenAI Deep Research** product at the model level, introducing an **intent clarification process**. Given a research request, GPT-5.6 does not start executing immediately; it first clarifies the user's true intent through a series of questions. For "Search for Bitcoin's trend over the past month and perform technical analysis," it would first ask: "Which data source do you prefer? Which technical indicators would you like analyzed?" This interactive clarification lets GPT-5.6 produce research reports that are more precise and better aligned with what the user actually needs.
>
> GPT-5.6 is a mature example of "Model as Agent"—web search, the code interpreter, and other built-in tools of the Responses API execute in a closed loop on the server; the orchestration loop moves from the client to the API server, which simplifies the client implementation. The model still emits standard tool calls; the client simply no longer has to build the "search—read—analyze" orchestration framework itself. Its most noteworthy aspect is the intent clarification mechanism: rather than executing a task immediately, the model first confirms what the user really needs, then formulates a research strategy. The gap between "what the user said" and "what the user actually wants" is addressed before execution begins.
>
> It is important to note that this experiment is not tied to any one vendor. Readers without OpenAI credits can reproduce it with providers that offer equivalent managed tools. For example, Alibaba Cloud Bailian's qwen3.7-plus Responses API also includes built-in `web_search` and `code_interpreter`; Kimi K3's Formula-managed search and `code_runner` provide the same class of capability.
>
> Figure 1-5 illustrates the complete architecture of native tool calling under the "Model as Agent" paradigm, along with the ReAct execution process of Kimi K3 and GPT-5.6 in real-world tasks.
>
> ![Figure 1-5: "Model as Agent" Architecture—Native Tool Calling](images/fig1-5.svg)

## Harness Engineering: Building Reliable Systems Around the Model

By now you understand how an Agent works at its core: an LLM runs the ReAct loop, guided by context, using tools to complete the task. The experiments above show that the basic mechanism works—and also expose how fragile it is. The model may hallucinate (invent tools or parameters that do not exist), pick the wrong tool, or fail to recover from an error. Between a working demo and a reliable product lies a substantial gap, and those fragilities are exactly what Harness Engineering exists to fix. The first half of this chapter answered what an Agent is; the second half answers how an Agent runs reliably in production.

The preceding sections established the core formula: **Agent = LLM + Context + Tools**. It describes the Agent's **internal composition**: reasoning engine, working context, and action interfaces. Harness Engineering adds a second, **implementation-level** view of the same system: treat the LLM as one core component (the Model), and call all the supporting code built around it the Harness. The two views are not rivals; they describe the same system at different levels of abstraction. We switch to the more general word "Model" because the principles of Harness Engineering apply to any model that can reason and call tools, not one particular kind. The core of the Harness is the original formula's "Context + Tools," plus three layers of safeguards: **Constrain** (what the Agent may and may not do), **Verify** (whether it did the thing correctly), and **Correct** (how to recover when it did not).

Expanded as an equation, the complete production-grade composition is:

> **Agent = Model + Harness**
>
> **Harness = Context management + Tool interfaces + Constraints + Verification + Correction**
>
> **Agent ↔ Environment**

A minimal demo needs only a Model and a Harness that can construct context and expose tools; a production system must add constraints, verification, and correction within that same boundary. For example, a refund Agent can place its policy in context, constrain calls with permission and amount rules, verify the result against database state, and retry or fall back after a timeout. Harness engineering studies precisely this runtime and governance code—outside the Model but inside the Agent boundary.

More precisely, the Harness is not everything outside the model: it is the runtime and governance layer **inside the Agent boundary and outside the Model**. It mediates the Model–Environment interaction but does not include the Environment itself. Tool definitions, call adapters, sandbox permissions and reset mechanisms belong to the Harness; files and processes that change inside the sandbox, external databases, web pages, users and the physical world belong to the Environment. Deployment location does not change this conceptual boundary. The core of the Harness is context management and tool interfaces, around which three types of engineering safeguards are built:

| Component | Responsibility and design principle | Practical examples | See chapters |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Context management** | Supplies relevant information. **Information sufficiency:** Give the Agent enough information to make an informed decision at each step. | System prompts, knowledge bases, Agent status bars, Sidecar bypass queries | Chapters 2 & 3 |
| **Tool interfaces** | Defines how the model can act. **Clear interfaces:** Use intuitive tool names, provide parameter examples, and explain each tool's limits. | MCP tools, code interpreter, search tools | Chapter 4 |
| **Constraints** | Defines what the Agent is allowed to do. **Fail-safe defaults:** Keep capabilities disabled until explicitly enabled, as with mobile app permissions. | Claude Code requires user authorization before tool execution by default. | Chapter 4 |
| **Verification** | Checks whether tool execution produced the correct result. **Input isolation:** Base security checks on structured data, such as fields returned by tools, rather than model-generated text that an attacker could influence through prompt injection. | Linting, type checks, validation of tool results | Chapters 5 & 6 |
| **Correction** | Recovers from errors or rolls back failed operations. Attempt recovery before presenting a failure to the user—for example, retry a failed tool call instead of showing an incomplete result. | Automatic retries, resuming generation, escalation to a human after repeated failures (a circuit breaker) | Chapters 2 & 5 |

The basic model control loop is shown in the following pseudocode:

```python
observation = Environment.observe()
trajectory = [observation]
while true:
	actions = Model(Harness.build_context(trajectory))
	if len(actions) == 0:
		break
	allowed_actions = Harness.constrain(actions)
	observation = Environment.apply(allowed_actions)
	if not Harness.verify(Environment):
		observation = Harness.correct(Environment)
	trajectory.append(allowed_actions, observation)
```

This skeleton deliberately omits implementation details. The complete API message loop appears in Chapter 2; tools and automatic verification are covered in Chapters 4 and 5, respectively.

Context and Tools let the Agent complete tasks—understand the task and act on it. Constrain, Verify, and Correct make sure it does so reliably and safely—not as something apart from Context and Tools, but as the engineering that keeps them working reliably in production. Along the maturity curve of Agent products, the emphasis between these two groups shifts.

Early Agent frameworks focused on Context and Tools: give the model tools, give it context, and let it complete tasks. Production-grade systems have shifted their center of gravity to Constrain, Verify, and Correct: making sure tool calls are safe, context is managed, and errors are recoverable.

Take Claude Code. The vast majority of its Harness code does Constrain, Verify, and Correct, not Context and Tools—the tools themselves (file read/write, command execution, search) are only a small part; the safeguards built around them are the true core. These mechanisms include:

- **Process State Management**: Tracks which step the Agent is currently executing
- **Multi-Layer Context Compression**: Automatically prunes information when there is too much
- **Permission Classification**: Controls which operations require user confirmation
- **Circuit Breaker**: Automatically stops retrying after repeated errors so one failing operation does not cascade through the whole system
- **Error Recovery Mechanisms**: Catches exceptions, rolls back to the last stable state, retries, or hands off to a human

**The industry is shifting from task completion to reliable task completion, making Harness Engineering the core competitive advantage of Agent systems.**

### From Prompt Engineering to Loop Engineering: The Evolution of Engineering Paradigms

Looking back at the development of AI application engineering, a clear evolutionary arc emerges:

**Prompt Engineering** was the first wave of innovation—improving output quality by refining the natural-language instructions fed to the model.

**Context Engineering** was the second wave—the realization that optimizing the prompt alone is not enough: all the information the model can see (system instructions, tool definitions, conversation history, external knowledge) has to be managed systematically.

**Harness Engineering** was the third wave—it widens the view from "what information the model receives" to "what kind of system the model runs in," taking in all infrastructure outside the model: constraint mechanisms, verification methods, feedback loops, error recovery.

**Loop Engineering** came next, widening the view from a single run to sustained autonomous operation across runs: who discovers the next piece of work, when to verify, and when the task counts as truly done (Chapter 10 develops this alongside multi-agent collaboration systems).

In July 2026, the industry began using **Graph Engineering** for a higher-level orchestration perspective: organizing Agent loops, deterministic programs, and human approvals into an explicit execution graph, where nodes provide capabilities, edges define routing and dependencies, and structured state travels along those edges and is persisted at key boundaries[^ch1-graph-engineering].

[^ch1-graph-engineering]: Josh C. Simmons used the name explicitly in his July 4, 2026 article *We Are Entering the Graph Engineering Phase*, summarizing it in terms of nodes, typed edges, and checkpointed state. On July 18, Peter Steinberger's question about whether the discussion had shifted from loops to graphs helped the name spread further. The practices predate the label: the official documentation for LangGraph, Microsoft Agent Framework, and Google ADK describes them as graph orchestration or graph-based workflows. See https://www.drjoshcsimmons.com/writing/we-are-entering-the-graph-engineering-phase, https://x.com/steipete/status/2078277297791189132, https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/overview, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/workflows/, and https://adk.dev/workflows/.

These five stages are not replacements but nested layers: Prompt Engineering is a subset of Context Engineering, which is a subset of Harness Engineering, which is a subset of Loop Engineering. Loop Engineering is, in turn, a subset of Graph Engineering: a single Agent loop forms one node in the execution graph. Each layer widens the engineer's scope of concern and influence beyond the last. **As models converge in capability and stop being the decisive differentiator, competitive advantage shifts to the engineering outside the model.**

Recent engineering practice supports this view. LangChain's work on Terminal Bench 2.0 (a benchmark evaluating an Agent's ability to complete complex tasks in a terminal environment) is a striking example: their Coding Agent improved from 52.8% to 66.5% (jumping from outside the top 30 to the top 5 on the leaderboard). What changed was not the model but the Harness—having the Agent check its own execution results, detect when it was stuck in a repetitive loop, and refine its reasoning strategy.

### Core Principles for Building Effective Agents

Based on Anthropic's experience, successful Agent systems follow three core principles[^ch1-anthropic-building-effective-agents].

**Keep it simple.** Start with the simplest solution and add complexity only when truly necessary. Direct API calls are preferable to complex frameworks; clear code is preferable to clever abstraction—every extra layer of abstraction is a new blind spot during debugging.

**Keep it transparent.** Show the Agent's planning steps, execution logs, and decision trajectory clearly. This is not just a debugging convenience; it is a precondition for user trust—an error inside a black box is hard to locate or fix from outside.

**Design a well-structured tool interface (ACI, Agent-Computer Interface).** ACI means designing the interface from the Agent's perspective—easy for the Agent to understand and use—rather than from the programmer's perspective, as in traditional APIs. Tool names and parameters should be intuitive, and wherever misuse is likely the design should make the mistake impossible from the start: a SIM card's notched corner lets it slide into the tray in only one orientation, and a microwave refuses to heat while its door is open. In manufacturing, this approach is known as **poka-yoke**, or **mistake-proofing**: designing products and processes to prevent mistakes or make them immediately apparent. It is used in the Toyota Production System.[^ch1-poka-yoke] A poorly designed tool can cause even the strongest model to fail repeatedly: the interface is the only channel between model and tool, and a vague interface gets amplified into systemic error.

[^ch1-poka-yoke]: Toyota UK, [“Poka-yoke – Toyota Production System guide”](https://mag.toyota.co.uk/poka-yoke/); American Society for Quality (ASQ), [“What Is Mistake Proofing?”](https://asq.org/quality-resources/mistake-proofing). Both describe mistake-proofing as preventing errors or detecting them as they occur.

[^ch1-anthropic-building-effective-agents]: Anthropic. "Building effective agents", December 2024. https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents

The next three sections address three freestanding but important topics in Harness engineering: model selection, orchestration patterns, and guardrails and safety. None belongs to the five Harness elements proper, but all are unavoidable in engineering practice.

### How to Choose a Model

> **实验 1-2 ★：Kimi K3 的原生智能体能力**
>
> 本实验展示了 **Kimi K3** 的原生智能体能力，它是"模型即智能体"范式的一个范例。Kimi K3 是一个混合专家（MoE）模型，参数量约为 2.8 万亿。MoE 可以看作一个专家团队：对于每类问题，系统只激活最适合的少数专家，而非整个模型，从而在保留能力的同时不承担完整的效率开销。Kimi K3 拥有 100 万词元的上下文窗口、原生视觉理解能力以及始终开启的"思考模式"。通过强化学习，它将工具调用的**决策策略**内化为原生能力：何时调用工具、调用哪个工具、传入什么参数，全部由模型自身决定，使其能够自主执行诸如网络搜索等任务。严格来说，被内化的是*何时以及如何调用*的决策；工具本身（如 `web_search` 和 `code_runner`）仍然作为 API 级别的内置工具在服务端执行。Kimi 通过一个名为 Formula 的服务端脚本引擎来运行这些官方工具。
>
> 关键观察在于：模型自主决定何时搜索、搜索什么，展现出真正的自主性；随着搜索结果返回，它会调整策略并判断信息是否充分。有一个常见的误解需要澄清：**强化学习赋予模型的是决策策略**，而非工具本身。它教会模型何时调用工具、选择哪个工具、传入什么参数、收到结果后是否继续，以及如何将数十甚至数百次调用串联成连贯的推理；这些*是否使用以及如何使用*的判断才被写入模型的权重。**工具及其执行由智能体框架或 API 内置提供**：`web_search` 和 `code_runner` 的实现、代码沙箱、以及发出调用和返回结果的基础设施全部位于模型之外。强化学习优化的是决策策略；它不会把搜索引擎或代码沙箱嵌入模型的权重中。因此，编排循环并未消失；它从客户端移到了服务端，而决策权则移入了模型内部[^ch1-2]。
>
> [^ch1-2]: 感谢读者 asdlem 通过 GitHub Issue #30 指出并澄清了这一区别：强化学习内化的是工具调用的决策策略，而非工具执行机制。参见 https://github.com/bojieli/ai-agent-book/issues/30
>
> Kimi K3 在智能体任务中的显著优势在于**长链工具调用的稳定性**——它能够维持 200 至 300 次连续工具调用，并始终保持连贯的推理，远超大多数模型在几十次调用后就开始退化的水平。K3 针对长周期编程和智能体工作负载进行了优化，发布了两个变体：K3 Max（用于对话和智能体任务）和 K3 Swarm Max（用于大规模并行处理）。作为一个开源模型，它在软件工程和智能体基准测试中与顶级闭源系统相匹衡——这证明了强化学习能够赋予模型原生的智能体能力。
>
> **实验 1-3 ★：GPT-5.6 的原生深度研究能力**
>
> 第二个实验使用 **OpenAI GPT-5.6** 来展示一个先进的模型如何借助 API 级别内置工具，在服务端为深度研究（Deep Research）闭合"搜索—阅读—分析"编排循环。GPT-5.6 有一个便利的特性是**自由格式工具调用（Freeform Tool Calling）**。传统上，模型调用工具时必须将每个参数序列化为严格的 JSON（一种结构化数据格式），就像按照僵硬的格式规则填写表格。自由格式工具调用（在 API 中通过 `type: "custom"` 的工具声明）允许模型直接向工具发送原始文本（如一段 Python 代码、一条 SQL 查询），完全避免了 JSON 转义。需要强调的是，这是 API 参数格式的演进，而非模型架构上的创新——客户端的工具调用循环（检测 `tool_calls` → 执行 → 返回结果）保持不变；只有参数从 JSON 字符串变为原始文本。
>
> GPT-5.6 配合 Responses API 的**网页搜索和代码解释器**内置工具，实现了深度研究的核心机制：模型可以自主搜索网络获取实时信息，并编写代码进行深入分析，实现"搜索 → 阅读 → 分析 → 再次搜索"的迭代研究过程。例如，面对"东盟十国首都之间的最短距离是多少？"这样的问题，GPT-5.6 会自动搜索每个首都的地理坐标，然后编写 Python 代码计算所有首都两两之间的大圆距离，最终找出距离最近的一对。类似地，在"搜索比特币过去一个月的走势并进行技术分析"这样的任务中，它可以从多个金融数据源获取实时价格数据，利用专业技术分析库计算移动平均线、RSI、MACD 等技术指标，生成可视化图表，并给出交易建议。
>
> 更重要的是，GPT-5.6 在模型层面内化了 **OpenAI Deep Research** 产品的设计理念，引入了**意图澄清流程**。面对研究请求，GPT-5.6 不会立即开始执行；它会先通过一系列问题澄清用户的真实意图。对于"搜索比特币过去一个月的走势并进行技术分析"，它会先问："您偏好哪个数据源？您希望分析哪些技术指标？"这种交互式澄清使 GPT-5.6 能够产出更精准、更符合用户实际需求的研究报告。
>
> GPT-5.6 是"模型即智能体"的成熟范例——网页搜索、代码解释器等 Responses API 内置工具在服务端闭环执行；编排循环从客户端移至 API 服务器，简化了客户端实现。模型仍然输出标准的工具调用；只是客户端不再需要自行构建"搜索—阅读—分析"编排框架。最值得注意的是其意图澄清机制：模型不是立即执行任务，而是先确认用户真正需要什么，再制定研究策略。"用户说了什么"与"用户实际想要什么"之间的鸿沟在执行开始之前就被弥合了。
>
> 需要说明的是，本实验不绑定于任何特定厂商。没有 OpenAI 额度的读者可以用提供等效托管工具的服务商复现。例如，阿里云百炼的 qwen3.7-plus Responses API 同样包含内置的 `web_search` 和 `code_interpreter`；Kimi K3 由 Formula 管理的搜索和 `code_runner` 提供同类能力。

## 驾驭层工程：围绕模型构建可靠系统

至此，你已经理解了智能体的核心工作方式：大语言模型运行推理-行动循环，由上下文引导，使用工具完成任务。上面的实验表明基本机制是可行的——同时也暴露了它有多么脆弱。模型可能产生幻觉（捏造不存在的工具或参数）、选错工具，或无法从错误中恢复。一个可运行的演示与一个可靠的产品之间存在相当大的差距，而这些脆弱性正是驾驭层工程所要解决的问题。本章前半部分回答了智能体是什么；后半部分回答的是智能体如何在生产环境中可靠运行。

前文确立了核心公式：**智能体 = 大语言模型 + 上下文 + 工具**。它描述了智能体的**内部构成**：推理引擎、工作上下文和动作接口。驾驭层工程为同一系统提供了第二个、**实现层面**的视角：将大语言模型视为一个核心组件（模型），将围绕它构建的所有支撑代码统称为驾驭层。两个视角并非对立，而是从不同抽象层次描述同一个系统。我们改用更通用的"模型"一词，是因为驾驭层工程的原理适用于任何能够推理和调用工具的模型，而非某一特定类型。驾驭层的核心是原公式中的"上下文 + 工具"，再加上三层保障：**约束**（智能体可以和不可以做什么）、**验证**（它是否正确完成了任务）、**纠正**（当它做错时如何恢复）。

展开为等式，完整的生产级构成为：

> **智能体 = 模型 + 驾驭层**
>
> **驾驭层 = 上下文管理 + 工具接口 + 约束 + 验证 + 纠正**
>
> **智能体 ↔ 环境**

最小的演示只需要一个模型和一个能够构建上下文、暴露工具的驾驭层；生产系统则必须在同一边界内增加约束、验证和纠正。例如，一个退款智能体可以将政策放入上下文，用权限和金额规则约束调用，对照数据库状态验证结果，并在超时后重试或回退。驾驭层工程研究的正是这些运行时和治理代码——位于模型之外，但在智能体边界之内。

更精确地说，驾驭层并非模型之外的所有东西：它是**位于智能体边界内、模型之外**的运行时和治理层。它介导模型与环境的交互，但不包括环境本身。工具定义、调用适配器、沙箱权限和重置机制属于驾驭层；沙箱内发生变化的文件和进程、外部数据库、网页、用户以及物理世界属于环境。部署位置不改变这一概念边界。驾驭层的核心是上下文管理和工具接口，围绕它们构建了三类工程保障：

| 组件 | 职责与设计原则 | 实际示例 | 参见章节 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **上下文管理** | 提供相关信息。**信息充分性：**在每一步给智能体足够的信息以做出明智决策。 | 系统提示词、知识库、智能体状态栏、Sidecar 旁路查询 | 第 2、3 章 |
| **工具接口** | 定义模型如何行动。**清晰的接口：**使用直观的工具名称，提供参数示例，说明每个工具的限制。 | MCP 工具、代码解释器、搜索工具 | 第 4 章 |
| **约束** | 定义智能体被允许做什么。**安全默认值：**能力默认关闭，直到显式启用，类似于移动应用权限。 | Claude Code 默认要求用户授权后才执行工具。 | 第 4 章 |
| **验证** | 检查工具执行是否产生了正确结果。**输入隔离：**基于结构化数据进行安全检查，例如工具返回的字段，而非模型生成的文本——后者可能被攻击者通过提示注入影响。 | Lint 检查、类型检查、工具结果校验 | 第 5、6 章 |
| **纠正** | 从错误中恢复或回滚失败的操作。在向用户呈现失败之前先尝试恢复——例如，重试失败的工具调用，而不是展示不完整的结果。 | 自动重试、恢复生成、多次失败后升级给人工处理（熔断机制） | 第 2、5 章 |

基本的模型控制循环如下方伪代码所示：

```python
observation = Environment.observe()
trajectory = [observation]
while true:
	actions = Model(Harness.build_context(trajectory))
	if len(actions) == 0:
		break
	allowed_actions = Harness.constrain(actions)
	observation = Environment.apply(allowed_actions)
	if not Harness.verify(Environment):
		observation = Harness.correct(Environment)
	trajectory.append(allowed_actions, observation)
```

该框架刻意省略了实现细节。完整的 API 消息循环见第 2 章；工具和自动验证分别在第 4 章和第 5 章中介绍。

上下文和工具让智能体能够完成任务——理解任务并采取行动。约束、验证和纠正确保它可靠且安全地完成任务——它们不是上下文和工具之外的附加物，而是让它们在生产环境中可靠运行的工程手段。在智能体产品的成熟度曲线上，这两组要素之间的重心会逐渐转移。

早期的智能体框架侧重于上下文和工具：给模型工具，给它上下文，让它完成任务。生产级系统已经将重心转移到约束、验证和纠正上：确保工具调用是安全的、上下文是被管理的、错误是可恢复的。

以 Claude Code 为例。其驾驭层代码的绝大多数属于约束、验证和纠正，而非上下文和工具——工具本身（文件读写、命令执行、搜索）只占很小一部分；围绕它们构建的保障机制才是真正的核心。这些机制包括：

- **进程状态管理**：跟踪智能体当前正在执行哪一步
- **多层上下文压缩**：信息过多时自动裁剪
- **权限分类**：控制哪些操作需要用户确认
- **熔断器**：重复出错后自动停止重试，防止单个失败的操作级联到整个系统
- **错误恢复机制**：捕获异常，回滚到最近的稳定状态，重试，或交由人工处理

**行业正从任务完成转向可靠的任务完成，这使得驾驭层工程成为智能体系统的核心竞争优势。**

### 从提示工程到循环工程：工程范式的演进

回顾 AI 应用工程的发展历程，一条清晰的演进脉络浮现出来：

**提示工程**是第一波创新——通过改进输入模型的自然语言指令来提升输出质量。

**上下文工程**是第二波——人们认识到仅优化提示词是不够的：模型能看到的所有信息（系统指令、工具定义、对话历史、外部知识）都需要系统化管理。

**驾驭层工程**是第三波——它将视野从"模型接收到什么信息"扩展到"模型运行在什么样的系统中"，纳入模型之外的所有基础设施：约束机制、验证方法、反馈循环、错误恢复。

**循环工程**接踵而至，将视野从单次运行扩展到跨运行的持续自主运行：谁来发现下一项工作、何时验证、以及任务何时才算真正完成（第 10 章与多智能体协作系统一起展开讨论）。

2026 年 7 月，业界开始使用**图工程（Graph Engineering）**这一更高层次的编排视角：将智能体循环、确定性程序和人工审批组织成显式执行图，其中节点提供能力，边定义路由和依赖，结构化状态沿这些边传递，并在关键边界处持久化[^ch1-graph-engineering]。

[^ch1-graph-engineering]: Josh C. Simmons 在其 2026 年 7 月 4 日的文章 *We Are Entering the Graph Engineering Phase* 中明确使用了这一名称，并以节点、带类型的边和检查点状态加以概括。7 月 18 日，Peter Steinberger 关于讨论是否已从循环转向图的提问进一步推动了该名称的传播。这些实践先于该标签出现：LangGraph、Microsoft Agent Framework 和 Google ADK 的官方文档都将它们描述为图编排或基于图的工作流。参见 https://www.drjoshcsimmons.com/writing/we-are-entering-the-graph-engineering-phase、https://x.com/steipete/status/2078277297791189132、https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/overview、https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/workflows/ 和 https://adk.dev/workflows/。

这五个阶段并非相互替代，而是层层嵌套：提示工程是上下文工程的子集，上下文工程是驾驭层工程的子集，驾驭层工程是循环工程的子集。循环工程又是图工程的子集：单个智能体循环构成执行图中的一个节点。每一层都将工程师的关注范围和影响力扩展到上一层之外。**当模型能力趋于趋同、不再成为决定性的差异化因素时，竞争优势便转移到模型之外的工程上。**

近期的工程实践印证了这一观点。LangChain 在 Terminal Bench 2.0（一个评估智能体在终端环境中完成复杂任务能力的基准测试）上的工作就是一个引人注目的例子：他们的编码智能体从 52.8% 提升到 66.5%（从榜单 30 名开外跃升至前 5）。改变的不是模型，而是驾驭层——让智能体检查自身的执行结果、检测是否陷入重复循环，并优化推理策略。

### 构建高效智能体的核心原则

基于 Anthropic 的经验，成功的智能体系统遵循三个核心原则[^ch1-anthropic-building-effective-agents]。

**保持简洁。** 从最简单的方案开始，仅在真正必要时才增加复杂度。直接的 API 调用优于复杂的框架；清晰的代码优于精巧的抽象——每多一层抽象，调试时就多一个盲区。

**保持透明。** 清晰展示智能体的规划步骤、执行日志和决策轨迹。这不仅是调试的便利，更是用户信任的前提——黑盒中的错误很难从外部定位或修复。

**设计结构良好的工具接口（ACI，智能体-计算机接口）。** ACI 意味着从智能体的视角设计接口——让智能体易于理解和使用——而不是像传统 API 那样从程序员的视角出发。工具名称和参数应当直观，在容易误用的地方，设计应使错误从一开始就不可能发生：SIM 卡的缺角使其只能以一个方向插入卡托，微波炉门打开时拒绝加热。在制造业中，这种方法被称为 **poka-yoke（防呆法）** 或 **防错（mistake-proofing）**：通过设计产品和流程来防止错误，或使错误立即可见。丰田生产体系中就采用了这一方法[^ch1-poka-yoke]。设计不当的工具即使是能力最强的模型也会反复失败：接口是模型与工具之间唯一的通道，含糊的接口会被放大为系统性错误。

[^ch1-poka-yoke]: Toyota UK，["Poka-yoke – Toyota Production System guide"](https://mag.toyota.co.co.uk/poka-yoke/)；American Society for Quality (ASQ)，["What Is Mistake Proofing?"](https://asq.org/quality-resources/mistake-proofing)。两者都将防错描述为防止错误发生或在错误出现时立即检测到。

[^ch1-anthropic-building-effective-agents]: Anthropic. "Building effective agents", 2024 年 12 月。https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents

接下来的三节讨论驾驭层工程中三个独立但重要的话题：模型选择、编排模式以及安全护栏与安全性。它们都不属于驾驭层的五个核心要素，但在工程实践中都是无法回避的。

### 如何选择模型

ANONYMOUS CHINESE Y:
> **实验 1-2 ★：Kimi K3 的原生智能体能力**
>
> 本实验展示了 **Kimi K3** 的原生智能体能力，它是"模型即智能体"范式的一个实例。Kimi K3 是一个约 2.8 万亿参数的混合专家（MoE）模型。MoE 可以理解为一个专家团队：面对每类问题，系统只激活最擅长的少数专家，而非整个模型，在保留能力的同时不必付出全额效率代价。Kimi K3 拥有 100 万 token 的上下文窗口、原生视觉理解和始终在线的"思考模式"。通过强化学习，它已将工具调用的**决策策略**内化为原生能力：何时调用工具、调用哪个工具、传什么参数，全部由模型自主决定，使其能够自主执行网络搜索等任务。更精确地说，被内化的是*何时以及如何调用*的决策；工具本身，如 `web_search` 和 `code_runner`，仍以 API 级内置工具的形式在服务端执行。Kimi 通过一个名为 Formula 的服务端脚本引擎运行这些官方工具。
>
> 关键观察是：模型自行决定何时搜索、搜索什么，展现出真正的自主性；它随着搜索结果的返回调整策略，判断信息是否足够。有一个常见误解值得澄清：**强化学习赋予模型的是决策策略**，而非工具本身。它教会模型何时调用工具、选择哪个工具、传什么参数、收到结果后是否继续，以及如何将数十甚至上百次调用串联成连贯的推理；这些*是否以及如何使用*的判断才被写入模型的权重。**工具及其执行由智能体框架或 API 内置机制提供**：`web_search` 和 `code_runner` 的实现、代码沙箱，以及发起调用和返回结果的基础设施，全部位于模型之外。RL 优化的是决策策略；它并不会把搜索引擎或代码沙箱嵌入模型权重。因此，编排循环并未消失；它从客户端移到了服务端，而决策则进入了模型[^ch1-2]。
>
> [^ch1-2]: 感谢读者 asdlem 通过 GitHub Issue #30 指出并澄清：RL 内化的是工具调用的决策策略，而非工具执行机制。参见 https://github.com/bojieli/ai-agent-book/issues/30
>
> Kimi K3 在智能体任务中的显著优势是**长链工具调用的稳定性**——它能够维持 200–300 次连续工具调用且推理始终连贯，远超大多数模型开始退化的几十次调用水平。K3 针对长周期编程和智能体工作负载进行了优化，发布了两个变体：K3 Max（用于对话和智能体任务）和 K3 Swarm Max（用于大规模并行处理）。作为开源模型，它在软件工程和智能体基准测试上与顶级闭源系统比肩——这是强化学习能够赋予模型原生智能体能力的证据。
>
> **实验 1-3 ★：GPT-5.6 的原生深度研究能力**
>
> 第二个实验使用 **OpenAI GPT-5.6**，展示一个先进模型如何在 API 级内置工具的支撑下，在服务端为 Deep Research 闭合"搜索—阅读—分析"编排循环。GPT-5.6 有一个便利的特性：**自由格式工具调用（Freeform Tool Calling）**。传统上，模型调用工具必须将每个参数序列化为严格的 JSON（结构化数据格式），就像填写一份有严格格式要求的表格。自由格式工具调用（在 API 中通过 `type: "custom"` 的工具声明）让模型可以直接向工具发送原始文本（一段 Python 代码、一条 SQL 查询），完全避免 JSON 转义。需要强调的是，这是 API 参数格式的演进，而非模型架构的创新——客户端的工具调用循环（检测 `tool_calls` → 执行 → 返回结果）保持不变；只是参数从 JSON 字符串变为原始文本。
>
> GPT-5.6 与 Responses API 的**网络搜索和代码解释器**内置工具配合，实现了 Deep Research 的核心机制：模型可以自主搜索网络获取实时信息，并编写代码进行深入分析，实现"搜索 → 阅读 → 分析 → 再搜索"的迭代研究过程。例如，面对"东盟 10 国首都之间最短距离是多少？"这样的问题，GPT-5.6 会自动搜索各首都的地理坐标，然后编写 Python 代码计算所有首都对之间的大圆距离，最终找出最近的一对。类似地，在"搜索比特币过去一个月的走势并进行技术分析"这样的任务中，它可以从多个金融数据源获取实时价格数据，利用专业技术分析库计算移动平均线、RSI、MACD 等技术指标，生成可视化图表，并给出交易建议。
>
> 更重要的是，GPT-5.6 在模型层面内化了 **OpenAI Deep Research** 产品的设计哲学，引入了**意图澄清流程**。面对一个研究请求，GPT-5.6 不会立即开始执行；它首先通过一系列问题澄清用户的真实意图。对于"搜索比特币过去一个月的走势并进行技术分析"，它会先问："你偏好哪个数据源？你希望分析哪些技术指标？"这种交互式澄清使 GPT-5.6 能够产出更精准、更符合用户实际需求的研究报告。
>
> GPT-5.6 是"模型即智能体"的成熟案例——网络搜索、代码解释器等 Responses API 的内置工具在服务端闭环执行；编排循环从客户端移到了 API 服务器，简化了客户端实现。模型仍然发出标准工具调用；客户端只是不再需要自己搭建"搜索—阅读—分析"的编排框架。其最值得关注的是意图澄清机制：模型不立即执行任务，而是先确认用户真正需要什么，再制定研究策略。"用户说了什么"与"用户真正想要什么"之间的差距，在执行开始之前就被弥合了。
>
> 需要注意的是，本实验不绑定任何特定厂商。没有 OpenAI 额度的读者可以用提供同等托管工具的服务商复现。例如，阿里云百炼的 qwen3.7-plus Responses API 同样包含内置的 `web_search` 和 `code_interpreter`；Kimi K3 由 Formula 托管的搜索和 `code_runner` 提供同类能力。

## Harness 工程：围绕模型构建可靠系统

至此你已经理解了智能体的核心运作方式：LLM 运行 ReAct 循环，以上下文为引导，使用工具完成任务。上面的实验表明基本机制是可行的——同时也暴露了它有多脆弱。模型可能产生幻觉（编造不存在的工具或参数）、选错工具，或无法从错误中恢复。从一个能跑的演示到一个可靠的产品之间存在相当大的鸿沟，而这些脆弱性恰恰是 Harness 工程要解决的问题。本章前半部分回答了智能体是什么；后半部分回答智能体如何在生产环境中可靠运行。

前几节确立了核心公式：**智能体 = LLM + 上下文 + 工具**。它描述了智能体的**内部构成**：推理引擎、工作上下文和动作接口。Harness 工程在同一系统上增加了第二个、**实现层面**的视角：将 LLM 视为一个核心组件（Model），把围绕它构建的所有支撑代码称为 Harness。两种视角并非对立，而是在不同抽象层次描述同一个系统。我们切换到更通用的"Model"一词，是因为 Harness 工程的原则适用于任何能推理和调用工具的模型，而非某一特定类型。Harness 的核心是原公式中的"上下文 + 工具"，外加三层保障：**约束（Constrain）**（智能体可以和不可以做什么）、**验证（Verify）**（它是否正确地做了事）和**修正（Correct）**（做错了如何恢复）。

展开为方程，完整的生产级构成为：

> **Agent = Model + Harness**
>
> **Harness = Context management + Tool interfaces + Constraints + Verification + Correction**
>
> **Agent ↔ Environment**

一个最小演示只需要一个 Model 和一个能构建上下文、暴露工具的 Harness；生产系统必须在同一边界内添加约束、验证和修正。例如，一个退款智能体可以将策略放入上下文，用权限和金额规则约束调用，对照数据库状态验证结果，并在超时后重试或回退。Harness 工程研究的正是这种运行时和治理代码——位于 Model 之外、Agent 边界之内。

更精确地说，Harness 并非模型之外的一切：它是**位于 Agent 边界内、Model 之外**的运行时和治理层。它介导 Model 与 Environment 的交互，但不包含 Environment 本身。工具定义、调用适配器、沙箱权限和重置机制属于 Harness；沙箱内变化的文件和进程、外部数据库、网页、用户和物理世界属于 Environment。部署位置不会改变这一概念边界。Harness 的核心是上下文管理和工具接口，围绕它们构建三类工程保障：

| 组件 | 职责与设计原则 | 实际示例 | 参见章节 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **上下文管理** | 提供相关信息。**信息充分性：**在每一步都给予智能体足够的信息以做出知情决策。 | 系统提示词、知识库、智能体状态栏、Sidecar 旁路查询 | 第 2、3 章 |
| **工具接口** | 定义模型如何行动。**清晰的接口：**使用直观的工具名称、提供参数示例、说明每个工具的限制。 | MCP 工具、代码解释器、搜索工具 | 第 4 章 |
| **约束** | 定义智能体被允许做什么。**默认安全（Fail-safe）：**在明确启用之前保持能力关闭，类似手机应用权限。 | Claude Code 默认在工具执行前要求用户授权。 | 第 4 章 |
| **验证** | 检查工具执行是否产生了正确结果。**输入隔离：**基于结构化数据（如工具返回的字段）做安全检查，而非可能被攻击者通过提示注入影响的模型生成文本。 | 代码检查（Linting）、类型检查、工具结果校验 | 第 5、6 章 |
| **修正** | 从错误中恢复或回滚失败操作。在向用户呈现失败之前先尝试恢复——例如，重试失败的工具调用，而非展示不完整的结果。 | 自动重试、恢复生成、多次失败后升级给人类（熔断器） | 第 2、5 章 |

基本的模型控制循环如下方伪代码所示：

```python
observation = Environment.observe()
trajectory = [observation]
while true:
	actions = Model(Harness.build_context(trajectory))
	if len(actions) == 0:
		break
	allowed_actions = Harness.constrain(actions)
	observation = Environment.apply(allowed_actions)
	if not Harness.verify(Environment):
		observation = Harness.correct(Environment)
	trajectory.append(allowed_actions, observation)
```

这个骨架刻意省略了实现细节。完整的 API 消息循环见第 2 章；工具和自动验证分别在第 4、5 章介绍。

上下文和工具让智能体能够完成任务——理解任务并据此行动。约束、验证和修正则确保它可靠、安全地完成任务——它们不是上下文和工具之外的附加物，而是让上下文和工具在生产环境中可靠运转的工程实践。沿着智能体产品的成熟度曲线，这两组要素的侧重点会逐渐转移。

早期的智能体框架聚焦于上下文和工具：给模型工具，给它上下文，让它完成任务。生产级系统已将重心转向约束、验证和修正：确保工具调用安全、上下文得到管理、错误可以恢复。

以 Claude Code 为例。其 Harness 代码的绝大多数在做约束、验证和修正，而非上下文和工具——工具本身（文件读写、命令执行、搜索）只是很小一部分；围绕它们构建的保障机制才是真正的核心。这些机制包括：

- **过程状态管理**：跟踪智能体当前正在执行的步骤
- **多层上下文压缩**：信息过多时自动裁剪
- **权限分类**：控制哪些操作需要用户确认
- **熔断器（Circuit Breaker）**：多次错误后自动停止重试，防止一次失败操作级联影响整个系统
- **错误恢复机制**：捕获异常、回滚到最后一个稳定状态、重试，或交由人类处理

**行业正从"完成任务"转向"可靠地完成任务"，使 Harness 工程成为智能体系统的核心竞争力。**

### 从 Prompt 工程到 Loop 工程：工程范式的演进

回顾 AI 应用工程的发展，一条清晰的演进脉络浮现：

**Prompt Engineering（提示词工程）** 是第一波创新——通过打磨喂给模型的自然语言指令来提升输出质量。

**Context Engineering（上下文工程）** 是第二波——认识到仅优化提示词不够：模型能看到的一切信息（系统指令、工具定义、对话历史、外部知识）都必须被系统地管理。

**Harness Engineering（Harness 工程）** 是第三波——将视野从"模型接收什么信息"扩展到"模型运行在什么类型的系统中"，纳入模型之外的所有基础设施：约束机制、验证方法、反馈回路、错误恢复。

**Loop Engineering（循环工程）** 随之而来，将视野从单次运行扩展到跨运行的持续自主运行：谁来发现下一项工作、何时验证、任务何时才算真正完成（第 10 章将与多智能体协作系统一起展开这一主题）。

2026 年 7 月，业界开始使用 **Graph Engineering（图工程）** 来描述更高层次的编排视角：将智能体循环、确定性程序和人工审批组织成一张显式执行图，其中节点提供能力，边定义路由和依赖关系，结构化状态沿这些边流动并在关键边界处持久化[^ch1-graph-engineering]。

[^ch1-graph-engineering]: Josh C. Simmons 在 2026 年 7 月 4 日的文章 *We Are Entering the Graph Engineering Phase* 中明确使用了这个名称，从节点、带类型的边和带检查点的状态三个维度加以总结。7 月 18 日，Peter Steinberger 关于讨论是否已从循环转向图的提问，进一步推动了这一名称的传播。这些实践早于这一标签：LangGraph、Microsoft Agent Framework 和 Google ADK 的官方文档都将它们描述为图编排或基于图的工作流。参见 https://www.drjoshcsimmons.com/writing/we-are-entering-the-graph-engineering-phase、https://x.com/steipete/status/2078277297791189132、https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/overview、https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/workflows/ 和 https://adk.dev/workflows/。

这五个阶段不是替代关系，而是嵌套的层次：Prompt Engineering 是 Context Engineering 的子集，Context Engineering 是 Harness Engineering 的子集，Harness Engineering 是 Loop Engineering 的子集。Loop Engineering 又是 Graph Engineering 的子集：单个智能体循环构成执行图中的一个节点。每一层都比上一层扩大了工程师的关注范围和影响力。**当模型能力趋于收敛、不再成为决定性的差异化因素时，竞争优势就转移到模型之外的工程上。**

近期的工程实践支持这一观点。LangChain 在 Terminal Bench 2.0（一个评估智能体在终端环境中完成复杂任务能力的基准测试）上的工作就是一个引人注目的例子：他们的编程智能体从 52.8% 提升到 66.5%（排名从前三十之外跃升至前五）。改变的不是模型，而是 Harness——让智能体检查自己的执行结果、检测自己何时陷入重复循环，并优化其推理策略。

### 构建高效智能体的核心原则

基于 Anthropic 的经验，成功的智能体系统遵循三条核心原则[^ch1-anthropic-building-effective-agents]。

**保持简单。** 从最简单的方案开始，仅在真正必要时才增加复杂度。直接调用 API 优于复杂的框架；清晰的代码优于巧妙的抽象——每多一层抽象，调试时就多一个盲区。

**保持透明。** 清晰展示智能体的规划步骤、执行日志和决策轨迹。这不只是调试的便利，更是用户信任的前提——黑盒内部的错误很难从外部定位或修复。

**设计良好的工具接口（ACI，智能体-计算机接口）。** ACI 意味着从智能体的视角设计接口——让智能体易于理解和使用——而非从程序员的视角，如传统 API 那样。工具名称和参数应当直观，在容易被误用的地方，设计应当从一开始让错误不可能发生：SIM 卡的缺口使其只能以一个方向插入卡托，微波炉门开着时拒绝加热。在制造业中，这种方法被称为 **poka-yoke（防错法）** 或 **mistake-proofing（防呆）**：通过设计产品和流程来防止错误或使错误立即显现。它被丰田生产体系所采用[^ch1-poka-yoke]。一个设计不良的工具可以让最强大的模型反复失败：接口是模型与工具之间唯一的通道，模糊的接口会被放大为系统性错误。

[^ch1-poka-yoke]: Toyota UK, ["Poka-yoke – Toyota Production System guide"](https://mag.toyota.co.uk/poka-yoke/)；American Society for Quality (ASQ), ["What Is Mistake Proofing?"](https://asq.org/quality-resources/mistake-proofing)。两者都将防错定义为防止错误或在其发生时立即检测。

[^ch1-anthropic-building-effective-agents]: Anthropic. "Building effective agents", December 2024. https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents
